synopsis:
The legend of Ne Zha comes to life through a modern retelling of its enduring mythic episodes. Rooted in a story widely known across China, the musical reimagines the classic tale of the Spirit Pearl’s reincarnation, Ne Zha’s defiant struggle against the sea, and the transformative image of rebirth through a lotus. These legendary moments unfold through contemporary theatrical language, combining Western modern music with performance forms that bring new energy to the ancient narrative while remaining faithful to its central mythology.

The show is not only a modern interpretation of a beloved Chinese legend, but also a story of reincarnation, resistance, and renewal. At its heart, it explores how timeless myth can be reshaped through contemporary music and performance.

synopsis:
Seventeen-year-old Xiao Liu, whose real name is Zhang Chengyi, chafes against every constraint placed upon him. His father, the traditional-minded quyi performer Zhang Zhongli, is determined that his son should inherit his artistic legacy, even as the distance between father and son has already left their relationship full of fractures. Then a performance poster throws their fragile balance into upheaval.

Against the backdrop of 2003, Xiao Liu turns to rock music to push back against the farewell performance of Jingyun dagu that his father has arranged for him, holding on to his own musical aspirations. Their conflict turns on an unresolved choice: whether to take up a family tradition or insist on a different dream.

The show is a story of a father and son confronting the tension between inheritance and self-determination. At its heart, it explores how music can become both a bond between generations and a means of rebellion.

synopsis:
Ye Bai, an emotional counsellor, finds that the capacity for a fluttering heart he once discarded has returned—not merely as a feeling, but as Xiao Bai, the embodiment of that very capacity. As Xiao Bai remains by his side, Ye Bai’s professional future is unsettled by the sudden arrival of the 99th female client, who insists that no one but the tarot blogger Lulu can solve her problem. The declaration casts a shadow over his prospects and sets Lulu up as his rival.

Determined to measure himself against Lulu, Ye Bai prepares for a rivalry he expects to be his own. Yet his plans take an unexpected turn when Xiao Bai, that same capacity now walking beside him in human form, falls in love with Lulu at first sight. Between a threatened career, a challenging rival, and a heart that has taken form outside his control, Ye Bai is drawn into an encounter where professional confidence and personal feeling become increasingly difficult to separate.

The show explores the tension between emotional expertise and the unpredictable force of being moved. Ultimately, it is a story of a discarded capacity for love returning, and of the complications that begin when the heart starts to act for itself.

synopsis:
Adapted from Feng Menglong’s Du Shiniang Angrily Sinks Her Treasure Chest: Du Shiniang, reduced to entering the Bureau of Music after her family fortunes collapse, entrusts her future to Li Jia, a young gentleman who falls in love with her at first sight. Hoping that he can lead her out of her desperate circumstances, she places her faith in their bond. With financial assistance from the scholar Liu Yuchun, the pair finally achieve what they have sought and set out by boat for Li Jia’s home. Yet during their journey, Sun Fu sways Li Jia, who sells Du Shiniang for one thousand taels of silver. Devastated by this betrayal, Du Shiniang takes her fortune of ten thousand in gold and throws herself into the river.

Ultimately, the show is a story of hope placed in love and shattered by betrayal. At its heart, it traces Du Shiniang’s desperate attempt to escape hardship, and the devastating price of Li Jia’s choice.

synopsis:
Luo Chuan, the son of a former minister, falls on hard times and finds himself at Zuixianlou, making a living by selling paintings. Simple-hearted and wholly devoted to perfecting his art, he is drawn into the predicament of a soul pact, sinking ever deeper into its consequences. At his side stands Chi Xun, Luo Chuan’s childhood friend and the descendant of a military family, who has risen to the frontier post of Commandant of the Pass. Though born into an official household, Chi Xun remains bound by affection, loyalty, and a promise that has never left his heart.

Elsewhere, Jing Yuan exists as a soul sealed within a painting. A fallen prince living in this disembodied form, he carries pride beneath an elegant exterior and calculates every turn of every scheme, reading the hearts of others with care. Yet amid the intricate game he has laid out, he has not foreseen that the most difficult move may be the one involving himself.

The show explores devotion, loyalty, and the price of pursuing what one holds most dearly. Ultimately, it is a story of souls caught between art, promises, and a fate that grows harder to escape.

synopsis:
Liu Yongfu leads the Black Flag Army through decades of war, from the campaign to resist France in support of Vietnam to the struggle against Japan in defence of Taiwan. Across eight scenes and nineteen original songs, the musical traces the army’s years of bloodshed and endurance amid the fires of conflict. Its story unfolds through a non-linear structure, moving across three temporal dimensions and two narrative threads rather than following a single chronological path. At the centre are Liu Yongfu and the force he commands, portrayed not as fixed historical types but as people shaped by hardship, resolve, and the demands of their times. The idea of returning home runs through the work as an emotional thread, accompanying the Black Flag Army’s long passage through warfare and sacrifice. As past and present intersect, the narrative connects personal longing with the wider weight of duty, placing the soldiers’ experiences within a history of resistance and national responsibility.

The show explores how the desire to return home can coexist with an inescapable obligation to the nation. Ultimately, it is not only a story of the Black Flag Army’s years of fighting, but also one of responsibility forged in war.
